Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan

units.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏
units.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan
units.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai

units.zh: 太祖一后三妃。
units.en: Taizu had one empress and three imperial consorts.
units.literal: Taizu had one empress and three consorts.

units.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州堯山人也，與太祖同里，遂以歸焉。
units.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan came from Yaoshan in Xing Prefecture. She and Taizu were neighbors, and he married her.
units.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai, was a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou. She and Taizu were from the same neighborhood, and he took her in marriage.

units.zh: 太祖微時，喜飲博任俠，不拘細行，后常諫止之。
units.en: In his early days Taizu loved wine, dice, and swaggering heroics, caring little for small proprieties; his wife often urged him to stop.
units.literal: When Taizu was still obscure, he delighted in drinking, gambling, and chivalric adventure, heedless of petty conduct; the lady often admonished and restrained him.

units.zh: 太祖狀貌奇偉，后心知其貴人也，事之甚謹。
units.en: Taizu's stature was striking and grand; his wife sensed in her heart that he was destined for greatness and treated him with scrupulous respect.
units.literal: Taizu's bearing was singular and imposing; in her heart the lady knew he was a man of eminence and served him with great deference.

units.zh: 及太祖即位，后已先卒，乃下詔：「故夫人柴氏，追冊為皇后，謚曰聖穆。」
units.en: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the lady had already died beforehand. He thereupon issued an edict: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously enfeoffed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."

units.zh: 淑妃楊氏
units.en: Imperial Consort Shu of the Yang clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort Shu, née Yang

units.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort Shu of the Yang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort Shu, née Yang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 父弘裕，真定少尹。
units.en: Her father Hongyu served as vice prefect of Zhending.
units.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice-Governor of Zhending.

units.zh: 妃幼以色選入趙王宮，事王熔。
units.en: As a girl she was selected for her looks and sent into the Zhao princely household to serve Wang Rong.
units.literal: While young the consort was chosen for her beauty and entered the palace of the Prince of Zhao, attending Wang Rong.

units.zh: 熔為張文禮所殺，鎮州亂，妃亦流寓民間，後嫁里人石光輔。
units.en: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli and Zhen Prefecture was thrown into chaos, she too was cast adrift among the people and later married a local man, Shi Guangfu.
units.literal: Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli; Zhenzhou fell into turmoil, and the consort too wandered among the common people, later marrying a townsman named Shi Guangfu.

units.zh: 居數年，光輔死。
units.en: Several years later Guangfu died.
units.literal: After several years Guangfu died.

units.zh: 太祖柴夫人卒，聞妃有色而賢，遂娶之為繼室。
units.en: After Taizu's wife from the Chai clan died, he heard that this consort was both lovely and worthy and took her as his next wife.
units.literal: When Taizu's Lady Chai died, hearing that the consort was beautiful and virtuous, he took her as his successor wife.

units.zh: 太祖方事漢高祖於太原，天福中妃卒，遂葬太原之近郊。
units.en: Taizu was then in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan. She died during the Tianfu reign period and was buried in the outskirts near the city.
units.literal: Taizu was then serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; in the Tianfu era the consort died and was buried in the suburbs near Taiyuan.

units.zh: 太祖即位，廣順元年九月，追冊為淑妃。
units.en: After Taizu became emperor, in the ninth month of Guangshun 1 she was posthumously installed as Imperial Consort Shu.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, in the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun she was posthumously enfeoffed as Imperial Consort Shu.

units.zh: 拜妃弟廷璋為右飛龍使，廷璋辭曰：「臣父老矣，願以授之。」
units.en: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon. Tingzhang declined: "My father is elderly; I would rather the appointment go to him."
units.literal: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon; Tingzhang declined, saying, "My father is old; I wish the post to be given to him."

units.zh: 太祖曰：「吾方思之，豈忘爾父邪！」
units.en: Taizu replied, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"
units.literal: Taizu said, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"

units.zh: 即召弘裕，弘裕老不能行，乃就其家拜金紫光祿大夫、真定少尹。
units.en: He immediately summoned Hongyu. Too frail to travel, Hongyu received at home the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and vice prefect of Zhending.
units.literal: He at once summoned Hongyu. Hongyu was too old to travel, so at his home he was invested as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and as Vice-Governor of Zhending.

units.zh: 太祖崩，葬嵩陵，一后三妃皆當陪葬，而太原未克，世宗詔有司營嵩陵之側為虛墓以俟。
units.en: When Taizu died he was interred at Song Mausoleum. The empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet fallen, so Shizong ordered officials to prepare vacant tombs beside the mausoleum until the time came.
units.literal: When Taizu died he was buried at Songling; the one empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet been taken. Shizong ordered the officials to prepare empty tombs beside Songling to await them.

units.zh: 顯德元年，世宗已敗劉旻於高平，遂攻太原，太原閉壁被圍，乃遷妃喪而葬之。
units.en: In Xiande 1, after Shizong had defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, he marched on Taiyuan. With the city shut up under siege, he had the consort's remains brought forward and buried.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiande, Shizong having already defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, then attacked Taiyuan. Taiyuan shut its walls and was besieged, whereupon he moved the consort's coffin and buried her.

units.zh: 貴妃張氏
units.en: Imperial Consort Gui of the Zhang clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort Gui, née Zhang

units.zh: 貴妃張氏，鎮州真定人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort Gui of the Zhang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort Gui, née Zhang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 祖記，成德軍節度判官、檢校兵部尚書。
units.en: Her grandfather Ji had been adjutant of the Chengde military commission and acting Minister of War.
units.literal: Her grandfather Ji was military adjutant of the Chengde command and Acting Minister of War.

units.zh: 父同芝，事趙王王熔為諮呈官，官至檢校工部尚書。
units.en: Her father Tongzhi had served Wang Rong of Zhao as memorial presenter and reached the post of acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Her father Tongzhi served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong as memorial presenter and rose to Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 熔死，鎮州亂，莊宗遣幽州符存審以兵討張文禮，裨將武從諫館於妃家，見妃尚幼，憐之，而從諫家在太原，遂以妃歸，為其子婦。
units.en: After Rong's death threw Zhen Prefecture into chaos, Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian from Youzhou against Zhang Wenli. The subordinate commander Wu Congjian was quartered at her family's house, took pity on the girl still in her youth, and—his own family being in Taiyuan—brought her home as a daughter-in-law.
units.literal: When Rong died Zhenzhou was in turmoil. Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian of Youzhou with troops to punish Zhang Wenli. The lieutenant Wu Congjian lodged at the consort's family home, saw that she was still young, and pitied her. Congjian's family was in Taiyuan, so he took the consort back and made her his son's wife.

units.zh: 久之，太祖事漢高祖於太原，楊夫人卒，而武氏子亦卒，乃納妃為繼室。
units.en: Years later, while Taizu was in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan, Lady Yang died and Wu's son died as well; Taizu then took the consort as his next wife.
units.literal: After a long while Taizu was serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; Lady Yang died, and Wu's son also died, whereupon he took the consort as successor wife.

units.zh: 太祖貴，累封吳國夫人。
units.en: As Taizu rose in stature she was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Lady of Wu.
units.literal: When Taizu rose in rank she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Wu.

units.zh: 太祖以兵入京師，漢遣劉銖戮其家，妃與諸子皆死。
units.en: When Taizu marched into the capital with his army, Later Han sent Liu Zhu to massacre his household; the consort and all his sons were killed.
units.literal: When Taizu entered the capital with troops, Han sent Liu Zhu to slaughter his household; the consort and all his sons perished.

units.zh: 太祖即位，追冊為貴妃。
units.en: After Taizu became emperor he posthumously installed her as Imperial Consort Gui.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Consort Gui.

units.zh: 德妃董氏
units.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong

units.zh: 〈（太祖子侗信侄守願奉超遜）〉
units.en: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉
units.literal: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉

units.zh: 德妃董氏，鎮州靈壽人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan was from Lingshou in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong, was a native of Lingshou in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 祖文廣，唐深州錄事參軍。
units.en: Her grandfather Wenguang had been recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.
units.literal: Her grandfather Wenguang was recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.

units.zh: 父光嗣，趙州昭慶尉。
units.en: Her father Guangsi served as magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.
units.literal: Her father Guangsi was magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.

units.zh: 妃幼穎悟，始能言，聞樂聲知其律呂。
units.en: From childhood she was exceptionally bright: as soon as she could talk, she could tell pitch and mode whenever she heard music.
units.literal: The consort was clever from childhood; as soon as she could speak, upon hearing music she knew its pitch and mode.

units.zh: 年七歲，鎮州亂，其家失之，為潞州牙將所得，置諸褚中以歸。
units.en: At seven, during the chaos in Zhen Prefecture, her family lost track of her. A Luzhou garrison officer seized her, tucked her into a sack, and took her away.
units.literal: At age seven, when Zhenzhou was in turmoil, her family lost her; a garrison officer of Luzhou obtained her, put her in a bag, and carried her off.

units.zh: 潞將妻嘗生女，輒不育，得妃憐之，養以為子，過於所生。
units.en: The commander's wife had borne daughters who never lived; when she got the girl she cherished her and raised her as a daughter, loving her even more than her own children.
units.literal: The Luzhou commander's wife had borne daughters who always failed to survive; obtaining the consort she pitied her and raised her as a daughter, loving her more than a child of her own flesh.

units.zh: 居五六年，妃家悲思，其兄瑀求之人間，莫知所在。
units.en: Five or six years passed. Her family mourned and missed her; her elder brother Yu searched the world for her, but no one knew where she was.
units.literal: After five or six years the consort's family grieved and longed for her; her elder brother Yu sought her among the people but did not know where she was.

units.zh: 潞將仕於京師，遇瑀，欣然歸之，時年十三。
units.en: The Luzhou commander was on duty in the capital when he met Yu and gladly gave her back; she was thirteen by then.
units.literal: The Luzhou commander was serving at the capital and met Yu; gladly he returned her—she was then thirteen.

units.zh: 瑀以嫁里人劉進超，進超亦仕晉為內職。
units.en: Yu married her to a local man, Liu Jinchao, who also held an inner-court post under Jin.
units.literal: Yu gave her in marriage to a townsman, Liu Jinchao; Jinchao also served Jin in an inner-office post.

units.zh: 契丹犯闕，進超歿於虜中，妃嫠居洛陽。
units.en: When the Khitans stormed the capital Jinchao died in their hands, and she lived as a widow in Luoyang.
units.literal: When the Khitans violated the capital Jinchao died among the invaders, and the consort lived as a widow in Luoyang.

units.zh: 漢高祖由太原入京師，太祖從，過洛陽，聞妃有賢行，聘之。
units.en: When Gaozu of Later Han entered the capital from Taiyuan, Taizu went with him. Passing through Luoyang he heard of her virtue and took her as his wife.
units.literal: Gaozu of Han entered the capital from Taiyuan; Taizu followed, passed through Luoyang, heard of the consort's worthy conduct, and betrothed her.

units.zh: 太祖建國，中宮虛位，遂冊為德妃。
units.en: When Taizu founded Later Zhou the empress's seat stood empty, and he installed her as Imperial Consort De.
units.literal: When Taizu founded the state the central palace was vacant, and he thereupon installed her as Imperial Consort De.

units.zh: 廣順三年卒，年三十九。
units.en: She died in Guangshun 3, at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: She died in the third year of Guangshun, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 妃兄三人：瑀官至太子右贊善大夫，玄之、自明皆至刺史。
units.en: She had three brothers: Yu rose to Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace; Xuanzhi and Ziming both became regional inspectors.
units.literal: The consort had three elder brothers: Yu rose to Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace; Xuanzhi and Ziming both reached the rank of regional inspector.

units.zh: 初，帝舉兵於魏，漢以兵圍帝第，時張貴妃與諸子青哥、意哥，侄守筠、奉超、定哥，皆被誅。
units.en: Earlier, when the emperor raised his army in Wei, Later Han besieged his residence. Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all executed.
units.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor raised troops in Wei, Han surrounded his residence with troops. At that time Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all put to death.

units.zh: 青哥、意哥，不知其母誰氏。
units.en: Who bore Qingge and Yige is not recorded.
units.literal: Qingge and Yige—whose mothers they were is unknown.

units.zh: 太祖即位，詔故第二子青哥贈太尉，賜名侗；
units.en: When Taizu became emperor he decreed that his late second son Qingge be posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he decreed that the late second son Qingge be posthumously granted Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;

units.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信；
units.en: that the third son Yige be posthumously made Minister of Works and given the name Xin;
units.literal: the third son Yige be posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the name Xin;

units.zh: 皇侄守筠贈左領軍衛將軍，以筠聲近榮，為世宗避，更名守願；
units.en: that the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously made general of the Left Army Guard—because jun sounded like "glory," it was changed for Shizong's taboo to Shouyuan;
units.literal: the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously granted General of the Left Army Guard; because jun sounded like glory, to avoid Shizong's taboo he was renamed Shouyuan;

units.zh: 奉超贈左監門衛將軍；
units.en: that Fengchao be posthumously made general of the Left Gate Guard;
units.literal: Fengchao be posthumously granted General of the Left Gate Guard;

units.zh: 定哥贈左千年衛將軍，賜名遜。
units.en: and that Dingge be posthumously made general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.
units.literal: Dingge be posthumously granted General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.

units.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月癸未，詔曰：「禮以緣情，恩以悼往，矧在友於之列，尤鐘惻愴之情。
units.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites arise from affection, and grace mourns the dead; how much more among brothers, where grief cuts especially deep.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, on the day guiwei of the fourth month of summer, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites follow affection; grace mourns the departed—how much more among brothers, where heartfelt grief is especially deep.

units.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗、贈司空信，景邊初啟，大年不登，俾予終鮮，實勤予懷。
units.en: My late brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the border war had barely begun did not live out their full span, leaving me brotherless to the end—a sorrow that truly weighs on my heart.
units.literal: The late imperial younger brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the frontier campaign had just opened did not reach full years, leaving me without brothers to the end—this truly weighs on my heart.

units.zh: 侗可贈太傅，追封郯王；
units.en: Tong shall be posthumously made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;
units.literal: Tong may be posthumously granted Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;

units.zh: 信司徒，𣏌王。」
units.en: Xin shall be posthumously made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi."
units.literal: Xin, Minister over the Masses, Prince of Qi."

units.zh: 又詔曰：「故皇從弟贈左領軍衞將軍守愿、贈左監門衞將軍奉超、贈左千牛衞將軍遜等，頃因季世，不享遐齡，每念非辜，難忘有慟。
units.en: He issued another edict: "My late cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, and posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, perished in these troubled times without reaching a full span of years. Whenever I recall their innocence, my grief will not be stilled.
units.literal: He issued another edict: "The late imperial cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, and others—lately, in a degenerate age, did not enjoy long life. Whenever I think how innocent they were, I cannot forget my grief.

units.zh: 守愿可贈左衞大將軍，奉超右衞大將軍，遜右武衞大將軍。」
units.en: Shouyuan shall be posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; and Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."
units.literal: Shouyuan may be posthumously granted Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 既而諸大臣以恩之所被，皆朝廷親近之臣，而宗室劉信及青州劉銖等皆國家元勛，必有不平之意，且外慮諸侯以朝廷有私於親近也，於是議及四方侯伯，普加恩焉。
units.en: Then the great ministers reflected that those favored were all the court's intimate ministers, while the imperial clansman Liu Xin, Qing Prefecture's Liu Zhu, and others were all founding merit of the state and would surely feel discontent. They also feared that feudal lords would think the court showed partiality to intimates. Therefore they discussed extending favor to the lords and princes throughout the realm.
units.literal: Then the great ministers reflected that those on whom favor had fallen were all the court's intimate ministers, while the imperial clansman Liu Xin and Qing Prefecture's Liu Zhu and others were all founding merit of the state and would surely feel discontent—and moreover they feared externally that feudal lords would think the court showed partiality to intimates—so they discussed extending favor to the lords and princes of the four directions universally.

units.zh: 己未，許州劉信加兼侍中，開封尹侯益進封魯國公，鄆州慕容彥超、青州劉銖並加兼侍中。
units.en: On jiwei, Liu Xin of Xu Prefecture was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu, and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou and Liu Zhu of Qing Prefecture were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
units.literal: On jiwei, Xu Prefecture Liu Xin was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu; Yunzhou Murong Yanchao and Qing Prefecture Liu Zhu were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 時鎔童幼，求援於燕；
units.en: Rong was still young and appealed to Yan for help.
units.literal: At that time Rong was still a child and sought aid from Yan.

units.zh: 鎔以匡威再來援己，致其失師，遣使迎歸府第，父事之。
units.en: Because Kuangwei had twice come to his aid and twice cost him his army, Rong sent envoys to welcome him to his mansion and treated him with the deference due a father.
units.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had twice come to aid him and thereby caused the loss of his army, sent envoys to welcome him back to the mansion and treated him as a father.

units.zh: 匡威為鎔城郛繕甲，指陳方略，視鎔如子。
units.en: Kuangwei fortified Rong's walls, readied his armor, laid out strategy, and treated Rong as a son.
units.literal: Kuangwei fortified the walls and readied armor for Rong, laid out strategy, and regarded Rong as a son.

units.zh: 會鎔過匡威第慰忌辰，匡威縞衣裹甲，伏兵劫鎔入牙城。
units.en: When Rong came to Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore mourning garments over his armor and used hidden troops to seize Rong and carry him into the headquarters.
units.literal: When Rong happened to visit Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore hemp mourning garments over armor and with hidden troops seized Rong and carried him into the headquarters.

units.zh: 鎔兵逆戰，燔東偏門，軍士呼噪登屋，矢下如雨。
units.en: Rong's troops fought back, burned the eastern gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the rooftops as arrows fell like rain.
units.literal: Rong's troops fought back, burned the east side gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the roofs; arrows fell like rain.

units.zh: 鎔僕墨君和亂中扶鎔登屋免難，而斬匡威以徇。
units.en: In the chaos Rong's servant Mo Junhe helped him climb onto a roof to safety, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.
units.literal: Rong's servant Mo Junhe in the chaos helped Rong climb onto a roof and escape harm, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed the head.

units.zh: 匡威親率軍應之。
units.en: Kuangwei personally led an army to his aid.
units.literal: Kuangwei personally led an army to respond.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 鎮之三軍，素忠於王氏，惡其所為。
units.en: The three armies of Zhenzhou had long been loyal to the Wang clan and despised his conduct.
units.literal: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang clan and hated what he was doing.

units.zh: 父洪裕，真定少尹。
units.en: Her father Hongyu served as Vice Magistrate of Zhending.
units.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice Magistrate of Zhending.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》云：父宏裕，少漁貂裘陂，有以二石雁授之者，其翼一掩左，一掩右，曰：「吾北嶽使也。」
units.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Yang Tingzhang, relates that his father Hongyu fished as a youth at Diaojiuqi Pond when someone presented him with two stone geese, one wing covering the left and one the right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."
units.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: his father Hongyu in youth fished at Diaojiuqi Pond; someone gave him two stone geese, one wing covering left and one covering right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."

units.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人。
units.en: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang, from Zhending in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 是年生女，為周太祖淑妃，明年生廷璋。）〉
units.en: A daughter was born that year—the future Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou—and Tingzhang was born the year after.)〉
units.literal: That year a daughter was born, who became Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou; the next year Tingzhang was born.)〉

units.zh: 安重誨保庇妃家，致其仕進，父母即以妃嫁於鄉人石光輔，不數年嫠居。
units.en: An Chonghui protected her family and helped them advance in office; her parents then married her to a townsman named Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.
units.literal: An Chonghui sheltered her family and secured their advancement in office; her parents thereupon married the lady to a fellow townsman, Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.

units.zh: 當河朔三鎮全盛之時，所屬封疆，制之於守帥，故韶顏美媛，皆被選於王宮。
units.en: When the three Hebei circuits were at their height, each garrison commander controlled his own domain, and fair-faced beauties were routinely drafted into princely palaces.
units.literal: When the three Hebei circuits were in full flower, their territories were controlled by the defending commanders, so fair-faced beauties were all selected for princely palaces.

units.zh: 是月，鎮州大將王德明殺其帥王熔，自稱留後，遣使來求援。
units.en: That month Wang Deming of Zhenzhou murdered Wang Rong, declared himself acting commissioner, and asked for help.
units.literal: That month, Zhenzhou great general Wang Deming killed his commander Wang Rong, styled himself retention commissioner, and sent envoys to seek aid.

units.zh: 宰臣敬翔請許之，租庸使趙岩等以為不可，乃止。
units.en: Jing Xiang favored acceptance; Zhao Yan and others refused, and the court declined.
units.literal: Chief minister Jing Xiang asked to grant it; Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan and others held it impossible, and it stopped.

units.zh: 庚戌，帝以北京馬步軍都指揮使、泗州防禦使、檢校太保劉崇為太原尹、檢校太尉，以北京馬步軍都虞候郭從義為鄭州防禦使、檢校太保，以北京興捷左廂都指揮使李洪信為陳州刺史、檢校司徒，以興捷右廂都指揮使尚洪遷為單州刺史、檢校司徒，以北京武節左廂都指揮使蓋萬為蔡州刺史，以武節右廂都指揮使周暉為濮州刺史，以保寧都指揮使朱奉千為隨州刺史。
units.en: On gengxu the emperor appointed Liu Chong prefect of Taiyuan, Guo Congyi defender of Zhengzhou, Li Hongxin prefect of Chenzhou, Shang Hongqian prefect of Shanzhou, Gai Wan prefect of Caizhou, Zhou Hui prefect of Puzhou, and Zhu Fengqian prefect of Suizhou, with the appropriate acting ranks.
units.literal: On the day gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry, Defender of Sizhou and Acting Grand Guardian, Yin of Taiyuan and Acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief registrar of the Northern Capital's horse and foot, Defender of Zhengzhou and Acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Northern Capital's Xingjie army, Prefect of Chenzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie army, Prefect of Shanzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning army, Prefect of Suizhou.

units.zh: 是月，周主威殂，養子晉王柴榮嗣立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Guo Wei died, and his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded him.
units.literal: That month Zhou ruler Wei died; his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 是月，周主榮殂，子宗訓立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: That month, Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 定哥贈左千牛衛將軍，賜名遜。
units.en: Dingge received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and the name Xun.
units.literal: Dingge was posthumously made General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and given the name Xun.

units.zh: 皇侄三人：守筠贈左領軍將軍，改名願；
units.en: Three imperial nephews: Shoujun received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Military Guard and was renamed Yuan;
units.literal: Three imperial nephews: Shoujun was posthumously made General of the Left Military Guard and renamed Yuan;

units.zh: 庚子，故吳國夫人張氏追贈貴妃；
units.en: On gengzi day, the late Lady Zhang of Wu was posthumously created Noble Consort;
units.literal: On the day gengzi, the late Lady Zhang, Lady of the State of Wu, was posthumously honored as Noble Consort;

units.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
units.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 時妃年尚幼，有幽州偏將武從諫者，駐騑於家，見妃韶令，乃為其子聘之。
units.en: She was still young when a subordinate commander from Youzhou named Wu Congjian was billeted at her home; struck by her grace, he betrothed her to his son.
units.literal: At the time the lady was still young; a partial commander from Youzhou, Wu Congjian, was quartered at her home, saw her fair and comely, and betrothed her to his son.

units.zh: 武氏家在太原。
units.en: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.
units.literal: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 天祐末，趙將張文禮殺王镕，以鎮州歸梁，莊宗命將符存審討平之。
units.en: At the end of Tianyou the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunshen to suppress him.
units.literal: At the end of Tianyou, the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong ordered the general Fu Cunshen to pacify it.

units.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州龍崗人，世家豪右。
units.en: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, born into the Chai clan of Longgang in Xingzhou, came from a family that had long ranked among the region's great houses.
units.literal: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, née Chai, was a native of Longgang in Xingzhou; her family were for generations eminent local magnates.

units.zh: 故夫人柴氏，代籍貽芳，湘靈集慶。
units.en: Lady Chai of old, her clan's fragrance handed down through generations, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.
units.literal: Thus Lady Chai, her clan's fragrance handed down, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.

units.zh: 既而有司上謚曰聖穆。
units.en: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.
units.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.

units.zh: 宜正號於軒宮，俾潛耀於坤象，可追命為皇后。
units.en: Let her receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly realm; she is posthumously invested as Empress.
units.literal: She should receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly trigram; she may be posthumously invested as Empress.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張永德傳》云：周太祖柴後，本唐莊宗之嬪御也。
units.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Zhang Yongde, states that Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.
units.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Zhang Yongde》: the Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.

units.zh: 太祖微時，在洛陽聞後賢淑，遂聘之。
units.en: While he was still obscure, he heard in Luoyang of her virtue and refinement and took her as his wife.
units.literal: When the Emperor was still obscure, in Luoyang he heard that the lady was virtuous and refined, and thereupon took her in marriage.

units.zh: 莊宗沒，明宗遣歸其家，行至河上，父母迓之，會大風雨，止於逆旅數日。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's death Mingzong sent her home; on the way to the Yellow River her parents came out to meet her, but a violent storm forced them to halt at an inn for several days.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Mingzong sent her back to her family; on the road she reached the river, her parents came to meet her, and they were stopped by a great storm at an inn for several days.

units.zh: 世宗皇帝即後之侄也，幼而謹願，後甚憐之，故太祖養之為己子。
units.en: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful even as a boy, he won her deep affection, and the Emperor therefore raised him as his own son.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful and prudent from youth, she pitied him deeply, so the Emperor raised him as his own son.

units.zh: 太祖即位，乃下制曰：「義之深無先於作配，禮之重莫大於追崇。
units.en: After he took the throne he issued an edict: "In depth of righteousness nothing precedes the bond of marriage; in weight of ritual nothing surpasses posthumous honor.
units.literal: When the Emperor took the throne he issued an edict saying, "In depth of righteousness nothing comes before taking a spouse; in weight of ritual nothing is greater than posthumous elevation.

units.zh: 太祖嘗寢，後見五色小蛇入顴鼻間，心異之，知其必貴，敬奉愈厚，未及貴而厭代。
units.en: Once while he slept she saw a small five-colored serpent slip between his cheek and nose; struck by the omen and sure he was destined for greatness, she honored him all the more—yet she died before he rose to power.
units.literal: Once when the Emperor was asleep, the lady saw a small serpent of five colors enter between his cheek and nose; her heart marveled at it, knowing he would surely become exalted, and she served him with ever greater respect, yet before he attained eminence she died.

units.zh: 顯德初，太祖神主入廟，以後祔於其室。
units.en: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, she was enshrined beside him in his chamber.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the lady was enshrined with him in his chamber.

units.zh: 後見之，驚曰：「此何人邪？」
units.en: The lady saw him and cried out in surprise, "Who is this?"
units.literal: The lady saw him and said in astonishment, "Who is this man?"

units.zh: 後曰：「此貴人也，不可失也。
units.en: She replied, "This man is destined for greatness; we must not let him slip away.
units.literal: The lady said, "This man is of noble rank; he must not be let go.

units.zh: 囊中裝分半與父母，我取其半。」
units.en: She split her purse in two, gave half to her parents, and kept the rest."
units.literal: She divided the contents of her purse in half for her parents and kept half for herself."

units.zh: 父母知不可奪，遂成婚於逆旅中。
units.en: Seeing they could not dissuade her, her parents consented and the wedding was held at the inn.
units.literal: Her parents knew they could not prevail, and the marriage was completed at the inn.

units.zh: 後異其人，欲嫁之，請於父母。
units.en: Struck by his bearing, she wished to marry him and pleaded with her parents.
units.literal: The lady thought him extraordinary and wished to marry him; she asked her parents.

units.zh: 太祖壯年，喜飲博，好任俠，不拘細行，後規其太過，每有內助之力焉。
units.en: In his prime he drank and gambled freely, loved bold adventure, and cared little for petty propriety; she checked his excesses and was a steady force within the household.
units.literal: In his prime the Emperor loved drinking and gambling, delighted in chivalric adventure, and did not trouble over small proprieties; the lady admonished him when he went too far and often gave him strength within the household.

units.zh: 太祖佐漢之初，屬聖穆皇后棄世，聞妃之賢，遂以禮聘之。
units.en: Early in his service to the Later Han, after Empress Shenmu's death, he heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his wife with full ceremony.
units.literal: At the beginning when the Emperor aided Han, as Empress Shenmu had passed away, hearing of the lady's virtue he took her in marriage with full rites.

units.zh: 太祖自聖穆皇后蚤世以來屢失邦媛，中幃內助惟妃存焉，加以結珮脫簪，率由令範。
units.en: Since Empress Shenmu's early death he had lost consort after consort; she alone remained to manage the inner household, and in every detail of dress and deportment she set the standard.
units.literal: Since Empress Shenmu's early death the Emperor had repeatedly lost consorts of the state; within the inner curtain she alone remained as household help, and moreover in tying sashes and removing hairpins she always followed the fine model.

units.zh: 故第二子青哥贈太保，賜名侗；
units.en: the late second son Qingge received the posthumous rank of Grand Guardian and the name Tong;
units.literal: the late second son Qingge was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the name Tong;

units.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信；
units.en: the third son Yige received the posthumous rank of Minister of Works and the name Xin;
units.literal: the third son Yige was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the name Xin;

units.zh: 故昭義節度使李嗣昭、故幽州節度使周德威、故汴州節度使符存審，並配饗莊宗廟廷。
units.en: Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and Fu Cunshen were given collateral offerings in Zhuangzong's temple.
units.literal: The late Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao, late Youzhou military commissioner Zhou Dewei, late Bianzhou military commissioner Fu Cunshen—all were collaterally offered in Zhuangzong's temple hall.
